title: Foundations
blurb: Alphabet, Numbers, Greetings, Verb To Be, Present Simple.

blocks.title: Nombre vs. sonido
blocks.en: Every letter has a NAME (how you say it in the ABC song) and one or more SOUNDS (how it works inside a word).
blocks.es: Cada letra tiene un NOMBRE (como se dice en la canción del abecedario) y uno o más SONIDOS (como suena dentro de una palabra).
steps: La letra C se llama /siː/ («si»), pero en cat suena /k/ y en city suena /s/.
La letra G se llama /dʒiː/ («yi»), pero en go suena /g/ y en giant suena /dʒ/.
Cuando deletreas (spelling) usas el NOMBRE: B-O-O-K, «bi-ou-ou-key».
blocks.tip: Al deletrear en voz alta, los angloparlantes dicen «double L» para LL y «capital B» para B mayúscula.

blocks.title: Vocal o consonante
blocks.help: Recuerda: solo A, E, I, O, U son vocales. Todas las demás son consonantes.

qs.q: Is E a vowel or a consonant?
qs.why: E es una de las cinco vocales: A E I O U.

qs.q: Is T a vowel or a consonant?
qs.why: T no está en A E I O U, así que es consonante.

qs.q: How do you say the letter G in English?
qs.why: G se llama /dʒiː/ («yi»). El sonido /g/ es otra cosa: go.
El final es U-V-W-X-Y-Z, así que después de V va W.

qs.q: How many letters does the English alphabet have?
qs.why: 26. El español tiene 27 porque incluye la Ñ; el inglés no la tiene.

qs.q: Which word starts with the sound /k/?
qs.why: Queen empieza con /kw/. City empieza con /s/ y giant con /dʒ/.

qs.q: What letter does DOG start with?
How do you spell BOOK out loud?
qs.why: Se usan los NOMBRES de las letras: B /biː/, O /oʊ/, O, K /keɪ/.

qs.q: Is the H silent in the word HOUSE?
qs.why: En inglés la H inicial casi siempre suena: /haʊs/. Excepciones: hour, honest.
Sí: A E I O U.

qs.q: Q is almost always followed by…
Which group is in the right order?
qs.why: L-M-N-O-P, el tramo rápido de la canción.

blocks.title: El patrón de las decenas
blocks.en: From 21 to 99 you say the ten, a hyphen, and the unit: twenty-one, forty-five, ninety-nine.
blocks.es: De 21 a 99 dices la decena, un guion y la unidad. No existe «twentyone» ni «twenty and one».
steps: 13-19 terminan en -TEEN: thirteen, fourteen, fifteen…
20-90 terminan en -TY: twenty, thirty, forty (¡sin U!), fifty…
100 = one hundred / a hundred. 101 = one hundred and one (UK).
blocks.tip: thirTEEN lleva el acento al final; THIRty al principio. Ese acento es la única diferencia audible entre 13 y 30.

blocks.hint: Toca una tarjeta para ver cómo se escribe con palabras.

blocks.title: Formal o informal: elige el registro
blocks.en: The greeting you choose signals distance. Good morning is safe with anyone; What's up? only works with friends.
blocks.es: El saludo marca la distancia social. Good morning sirve con cualquiera; What's up? solo con amigos.
steps: Good morning: hasta las 12:00. Good afternoon: de 12:00 a ~18:00. Good evening: al llegar de noche.
Good night NO es un saludo: es despedida al ir a dormir.
Con desconocidos y en el trabajo, empieza formal y baja de registro si la otra persona lo hace.

topics.label: Verb To Be
topics.title: Verb To Be
topics.kicker: am · is · are — el verbo más usado del inglés

blocks.title: Una forma para cada persona
blocks.en: To be has three present forms: am (I), is (he/she/it), are (you/we/they). English needs the subject; Spanish does not.
blocks.es: To be tiene tres formas en presente: am, is, are. En inglés el sujeto es obligatorio: no se dice «Is a teacher», sino «She is a teacher».
steps: Elige la forma según el sujeto: I am, he is, they are.
Para negar, añade not detrás del verbo: She is not a nurse.
Para preguntar, invierte verbo y sujeto: Is she a nurse?
blocks.tip: Contracciones: I'm, you're, he's, we're, they're. En negativo: isn't, aren't. «Amn't» no existe: se usa I'm not.

blocks.title: Los cinco usos de TO BE

items.es: Edad — en español se usa «tener», en inglés «to be».

blocks.title: Dos tipos de pregunta
blocks.en: Yes/No questions start with the verb. WH- questions start with a question word, then the verb.
blocks.es: Las preguntas de sí/no empiezan por el verbo. Las WH- empiezan por la palabra interrogativa y luego el verbo.
steps: Yes/No: Are you tired?  →  Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.
WH-: Where are you from?  →  I'm from Chile.
Nunca uses do/does con to be: «Do you are tired?» es incorrecto.

blocks.title: Auxiliar, no verbo principal
blocks.en: Do and does build questions and negatives in the present simple. The main verb goes back to its base form.
blocks.es: Do y does sirven para preguntar y negar en presente simple. El verbo principal vuelve a su forma base, sin -s.
steps: DO con I, you, we, they. DOES con he, she, it.
La -s de la tercera persona se «muda» al auxiliar: He works → Does he work?
Error clásico: «Does she works?» — la -s solo puede estar en un sitio.
blocks.tip: Do también puede ser verbo principal: I do my homework. Y entonces convive con el auxiliar: Does he do his homework?

blocks.title: Cuándo se usa
blocks.en: Use the present simple for habits, permanent facts and timetables — not for what is happening right now.
blocks.es: Se usa para hábitos, hechos permanentes y horarios. Para lo que ocurre ahora mismo se usa el present continuous.
blocks.formula: I / you / we / they + verb  ·  he / she / it + verb + s
steps: Hábito: I get up at seven every day.
Hecho: Water boils at 100 °C.
Horario: The train leaves at 8:15.

blocks.title: Reading: A Typical Day
paras: Carlos is a university student. He wakes up at 7 o'clock every morning. He does not wake up late because he has class at 8. He takes a shower and eats breakfast. He usually eats arepas and eggs.

In the evening, Carlos does his homework and reads his textbooks. He sometimes plays video games. He goes to bed at 11 PM. On weekends, he doesn't study — he hangs out with his friends.

topics.label: Possessives
topics.title: Possessive Adjectives
topics.kicker: my · your · his · her · its · our · their

blocks.title: El posesivo concuerda con el DUEÑO
blocks.en: In English the possessive agrees with the owner, not with the object. It never takes a plural -s.
blocks.es: En inglés el posesivo concuerda con el dueño, no con el objeto. Y nunca lleva -s de plural.
blocks.formula: his car · his cars   ·   her car · her cars
steps: Su coche (de él) = his car. Su coche (de ella) = her car.
Sus coches (de él) = his cars — el posesivo no cambia.
«Their friends», no «Theirs friends».
blocks.tip: its = posesivo (its tail). it's = it is. Es el error de ortografía más común del inglés.

items.en: This is my brother. His name is Dan.
The dog is wagging its tail.

blocks.title: Reading: Family Photo
paras: Look at this family photo. Next to me is my mother. Her name is Rosa. On the left is my father. His name is Alberto. Those are my parents.
The little girl in front is my sister, Sofia. Her dress is pink. The boy next to her is my brother, Marco. His shirt is blue. We love our family very much.
The dog in the photo is named Lucky. Its fur is brown and white. Lucky is our pet. Its favourite toy is a red ball. In the background, you can see our house. It is a big yellow house with a garden.

blocks.title: Cómo se habla del trabajo
blocks.en: Professions in the singular always take a or an: I am a nurse, she is an engineer.
blocks.es: Las profesiones en singular llevan siempre a / an: I am a nurse, she is an engineer. En español no se usa artículo, y de ahí el error.
blocks.formula: What do you do?  →  I'm a / an + job
steps: an va antes de sonido vocálico: an artist, an engineer, an hour.
«I am teacher» es incorrecto; «I am a teacher» es correcto.
Para el lugar: I work in a hospital / for a bank / as a designer.

topics.label: Prepositions
topics.title: Prepositions of Time & Place
topics.kicker: in · on · at — y las de lugar

blocks.title: in, on, at: de grande a pequeño
blocks.en: For both time and place, IN is the biggest container, ON is a surface or a date, AT is a precise point.
blocks.es: Tanto en tiempo como en lugar: IN es lo más grande, ON es una superficie o una fecha, AT es un punto exacto.
steps: Tiempo: in (meses, años, estaciones), on (días y fechas), at (horas y momentos).
Lugar: in (país, ciudad, habitación), on (superficie, calle, planta), at (dirección exacta, evento).
Excepciones fijas: at night, at the weekend (UK), on the weekend (US).

blocks.title: a o an: manda el SONIDO
blocks.en: Use an before a vowel SOUND, not before a vowel letter. That is why we say a university and an hour.
blocks.es: Se usa an delante de SONIDO vocálico, no de letra vocal. Por eso a university (suena «yu») y an hour (la h es muda).
blocks.formula: a + consonant sound  ·  an + vowel sound
steps: a book, a car, a house — sonido consonántico.
an apple, an egg, an umbrella — sonido vocálico.
Casos trampa: a European, a one-way street, an MP3, an X-ray.
blocks.tip: Con siglas cuenta cómo se lee la letra: an MBA («em»), a UFO («yu»).

blocks.title: Primera mención vs. segunda mención
blocks.en: Use a/an the first time you mention something, and the when the listener already knows which one you mean.
blocks.es: Se usa a/an la primera vez que mencionas algo, y the cuando ya se sabe de cuál hablas.
blocks.formula: I saw a dog. The dog was black.
steps: a/an: uno cualquiera, primera vez.
the: ese en concreto, único o ya conocido — the sun, the President, the book I bought.
Ø (sin artículo): plurales e incontables en sentido general — I like coffee. Dogs are loyal.
blocks.tip: No se usa the con nombres de países (excepto the UK, the USA, the Netherlands), idiomas, comidas ni deportes: I speak Spanish, I play tennis.

blocks.title: Afirmativo vs. negativo/pregunta
blocks.en: Some goes in affirmative sentences, any in negatives and questions. Both work with plurals and uncountables.
blocks.es: Some va en frases afirmativas; any en negativas y preguntas. Los dos se usan con plurales e incontables.
steps: I have some money. → afirmativo.
I don't have any money. → negativo.
Do you have any questions? → pregunta.

blocks.title: Delante del sustantivo y sin plural
blocks.en: Adjectives go before the noun and never change form: two red cars, not two reds cars.
blocks.es: El adjetivo va delante del sustantivo y nunca cambia: two red cars, no «two reds cars».
steps: a big house — delante del sustantivo.
The house is big. — después del verbo to be.
Sin concordancia: happy children, happy child.
blocks.tip: Orden aproximado cuando hay varios: opinión → tamaño → edad → forma → color → origen → material. «A beautiful small old round black Italian wooden table.»

blocks.en: Frequency adverbs go before the main verb, but after the verb to be.

blocks.formula: S + adverb + verb   ·   S + be + adverb
steps: I always drink tea. → antes del verbo principal.

blocks.title: Corto con -er, largo con more
blocks.en: One-syllable adjectives take -er; adjectives of three syllables or more take more. Two-syllable adjectives split.
blocks.es: Los adjetivos de una sílaba llevan -er; los de tres o más llevan more. Los de dos sílabas se reparten.
blocks.formula: adj + er + than   ·   more + adj + than
steps: tall → taller than
expensive → more expensive than
happy → happier than (acaba en -y → ier)
big → bigger than (dobla la consonante final)
blocks.tip: Irregulares imprescindibles: good → better, bad → worse, far → further/farther.

blocks.title: Siempre con THE
blocks.en: Superlatives compare one thing with a whole group and almost always take the.
blocks.es: El superlativo compara con todo un grupo y casi siempre lleva the.
blocks.formula: the + adj + est   ·   the most + adj
steps: the tallest building in the world
the most expensive restaurant in town
Detrás del superlativo se usa in con lugares y of con grupos: the best in the class, the best of all.

blocks.title: Adjetivo describe cosas, adverbio describe acciones
blocks.en: Most adverbs of manner are the adjective plus -ly. They describe the verb, not the noun.
blocks.es: La mayoría de adverbios de modo son el adjetivo + -ly. Describen al verbo, no al sustantivo.
steps: She is a careful driver. (adjetivo + sustantivo)
She drives carefully. (verbo + adverbio)
Irregulares: good → well, fast → fast, hard → hard.

title: Actions & Abilities
blurb: Can/can't, present continuous, imperatives, would like.

blocks.title: Un modal invariable
blocks.en: Can never changes form and is always followed by the base verb: no -s, no to.
blocks.es: Can no cambia nunca y va siempre con el verbo en forma base: sin -s y sin to.
steps: I can swim. He can swim. — sin -s en la tercera persona.
Negativo: cannot → can't.
Pregunta: Can you help me? — sin do.
blocks.tip: Pronunciación: en afirmativo can es débil /kən/; en negativo can't se alarga /kɑːnt/. Ese alargamiento es la pista para distinguirlos.

blocks.title: Ahora mismo o temporalmente
blocks.en: Use the present continuous for actions happening now or temporary situations around now.
blocks.es: Se usa para acciones que pasan ahora o situaciones temporales de este momento de la vida.
steps: Ahora: I'm working. Look! It's raining.
Temporal: She is living in Lisbon this year.
Planes fijos futuros: We are flying to Rome on Friday.

blocks.title: Rutina contra momento
blocks.en: Present simple = routines and permanent facts. Present continuous = right now and temporary.
blocks.es: Present simple = rutina y hechos permanentes. Present continuous = ahora y temporal.

blocks.en: The imperative is just the base verb. The negative adds don't.
blocks.es: El imperativo es el verbo base, sin sujeto. El negativo añade don't.
steps: Open the door. / Sit down, please.
Don't touch that. / Don't be late.

blocks.title: Dos patrones que hay que memorizar
blocks.en: Some verbs are followed by to + verb, others by verb-ing. A few accept both.
blocks.es: Unos verbos piden to + verbo y otros verbo-ing. Unos pocos aceptan las dos formas.

verbo-ing: enjoy, like, love, hate, finish, stop, mind, suggest, avoid.

blocks.title: Sujeto delante, objeto detrás
blocks.en: Subject pronouns do the action; object pronouns receive it and go after the verb or a preposition.
blocks.es: El pronombre sujeto hace la acción; el de objeto la recibe y va después del verbo o de una preposición.
blocks.formula: I see her.   ·   She sees me.
steps: Después del verbo: I know him.
Después de preposición: with us, for them, to me.
En inglés el objeto no se puede omitir: «I like» está incompleto; «I like it» es correcto.

blocks.title: El dueño va primero
blocks.en: English marks the owner with 's and puts it before the thing owned. The order is the opposite of Spanish.
blocks.es: El inglés marca al dueño con 's y lo pone delante de lo poseído. El orden es el contrario del español.
steps: El coche de María → Maria's car.
Plural que ya acaba en -s → solo apóstrofo: my parents' house.
Plural irregular → 's normal: the children's toys.
Para cosas se prefiere of: the door of the car / the car door.

blocks.title: Have got y have significan lo mismo
blocks.en: Have got is common in British English for possession. American English prefers have with do/does.
blocks.es: Have got es típico del inglés británico para posesión. El americano prefiere have con do/does.
steps: I've got a car. = I have a car.
Negativo: I haven't got a car. / I don't have a car.
Pregunta: Have you got a car? / Do you have a car?

blocks.title: Concuerda con lo que viene después
blocks.en: There is goes with singular and uncountable nouns; there are with plurals. The verb agrees with the noun that follows.
blocks.es: There is va con singular e incontables; there are con plurales. El verbo concuerda con el sustantivo que le sigue.
blocks.formula: There is + singular   ·   There are + plural
steps: There is a book on the table.
There are three books on the table.
There is some milk. — incontable → is.
En listas mixtas manda el primer elemento: There is a sofa and two chairs.
blocks.tip: No confundas there (existencia) con they're (they are) ni con their (posesivo). Se pronuncian casi igual.

blocks.title: there is / there are

blocks.title: There is / there are
blocks.help: El verbo concuerda con lo que sigue, no con «there».

qs.why: La existencia se expresa con there are.

blocks.title: Cada conector marca una relación
blocks.en: Conjunctions join ideas and tell the reader how they relate: addition, contrast, choice, cause or result.
blocks.es: Los conectores unen ideas y explican la relación: suma, contraste, elección, causa o consecuencia.
steps: and: suma. I like tea and coffee.
but: contraste. It's cheap but good.
or: alternativa. Tea or coffee?
because: causa. I'm tired because I worked late.
so: consecuencia. I was tired, so I went to bed.
blocks.tip: because responde a «¿por qué?»; so introduce el resultado. La misma idea, en orden inverso.

head: Conector
Relación
Ejemplo

It rained, so we stayed home.

blocks.title: El inglés es rígido con el orden
blocks.en: The basic order is Subject – Verb – Object, then place, then time. Adverbs of frequency sit before the main verb.
blocks.es: El orden básico es Sujeto – Verbo – Objeto, después lugar y después tiempo. Los adverbios de frecuencia van antes del verbo principal.
steps: I read a book in the park every evening.
Nunca separes el verbo de su objeto: «I read every day a book» es incorrecto.
El tiempo puede ir al principio para dar énfasis: Every evening, I read a book.

title: Past Tense
blurb: Was/were, past simple regular and irregular, negatives and questions.

blocks.title: Solo dos formas
blocks.en: The past of to be has just two forms: was for I/he/she/it, were for you/we/they.
blocks.es: El pasado de to be tiene solo dos formas: was para I/he/she/it y were para you/we/they.
steps: Afirmativo: I was tired. They were happy.
Negativo: wasn't / weren't.
Pregunta: Was he there? Were you at home?
blocks.tip: En condicionales irreales se usa were con todos: «If I were you…». Es la forma culta y la que se enseña.

items.en: two days ago · a long time ago

items.es: Con años y décadas se usa in.

blocks.title: Reading: A Long Time Ago
paras: My grandfather was a farmer. He was born in a small village near Ibagué in 1940. Life was simple but happy. His parents were very hardworking. There were no computers or mobile phones — people were much more connected to nature.

My grandmother was a teacher. She was very patient and kind. Her students were always happy to see her. The school wasn't big — there were only twenty children in each class. "Those were the best days of my life," she always says.

blocks.title: was / were
blocks.help: I, he, she, it → was. You, we, they → were.

blocks.title: Pasado de to be
blocks.help: Cuenta el sujeto y busca los marcadores temporales.

blocks.title: -ed para todos los sujetos
blocks.en: Regular verbs add -ed and the form is the same for every subject. Irregular verbs must be memorised.
blocks.es: Los verbos regulares añaden -ed y la forma es igual para todos los sujetos. Los irregulares hay que memorizarlos.
steps: work → worked, play → played.
-e final: like → liked. Consonante + y: study → studied.
Vocal + consonante tónica: stop → stopped, plan → planned.
blocks.tip: La -ed se pronuncia de tres maneras: /t/ en worked, /d/ en played, /ɪd/ en wanted (solo tras t o d).

Tras t o d, la -ed suena /ɪd/.

blocks.title: DID se lleva el pasado
blocks.en: In negatives and questions the auxiliary did carries the past, so the main verb goes back to its base form.
blocks.es: En negativas y preguntas el auxiliar did lleva el pasado, así que el verbo principal vuelve a la forma base.
blocks.formula: Did + subject + base verb?   ·   didn't + base verb
steps: I went → I didn't go. Did you go?
Error clásico: «I didn't went» — el pasado ya está en did.
Con to be no se usa did: Was he there?, no «Did he be there?».

title: Future & Plans
blurb: Will/shall, be going to, much/many/a lot, quantifiers.

blocks.title: El futuro que se decide al hablar
blocks.en: Will is for decisions made at the moment of speaking, predictions, promises and offers. It never changes form.
blocks.es: Will se usa para decisiones tomadas en el momento, predicciones, promesas y ofrecimientos. No cambia nunca de forma.
blocks.formula: will + base verb   ·   won't + base verb
steps: Decisión inmediata: The phone is ringing — I'll get it.
Predicción: It will rain tomorrow.
Promesa: I'll help you.
Ofrecimiento con Shall I…?: Shall I open the window?
blocks.tip: Shall solo se usa hoy en preguntas con I/we: Shall I…? Shall we…? En el resto suena antiguo.

blocks.title: Will en contexto
blocks.help: ¿Es una decisión de ahora, una predicción o un plan ya hecho?

blocks.title: El futuro ya decidido
blocks.en: Be going to expresses plans decided before speaking and predictions based on evidence you can see.
blocks.es: Be going to expresa planes decididos antes de hablar y predicciones basadas en pruebas visibles.
blocks.formula: am / is / are + going to + base verb
steps: Plan: I'm going to study medicine.
Evidencia: Look at those clouds — it's going to rain.
Con verbos de movimiento se prefiere el continuous: I'm going to the cinema (no «going to go»).

blocks.title: will o going to
blocks.help: ¿Estaba decidido antes o lo decides ahora?

blocks.title: Elige el futuro
blocks.help: Busca la pista: pruebas, plan previo, o decisión espontánea.

blocks.title: El sustantivo decide el cuantificador
blocks.en: Many goes with countable plurals, much with uncountables. A lot of works with both.
blocks.es: Many va con contables plurales y much con incontables. A lot of sirve para los dos.
blocks.formula: many books · much water · a lot of both
steps: How many students are there?
How much time do we have?
much y many aparecen sobre todo en negativas y preguntas; en afirmativas se prefiere a lot of.
blocks.tip: «There are much people» es un error frecuente: people es contable plural, así que many people o a lot of people.

items.es: a few = unos cuantos (positivo). few = pocos (negativo).
a little = un poco. little = muy poco, casi nada.
enough = suficiente; va antes del sustantivo.

blocks.title: much / many / a lot of
blocks.help: Mira si el sustantivo es contable plural o incontable.

items.why: En afirmativa se prefiere a lot of.

blocks.title: Cuantificadores
blocks.help: Contable plural → many/a few. Incontable → much/a little.
